stem: Draw a graph of stopping potential against frequency for two metals A and B ($\phi_A<\phi_B$). What do the slope and the intercept on the frequency axis represent?
model_answer:
Two parallel straight lines; A's line starts at a lower threshold frequency than B's. [1]
Slope $=h/e$ (same for all metals); intercept on the frequency axis $=$ threshold frequency $\nu_0=\phi_0/h$. [1]

stem: An electron and a proton have the same kinetic energy. Find the ratio of their de Broglie wavelengths. ($m_p=1836\,m_e$)
model_answer:
$\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mK}}$, so at equal $K$, $\dfrac{\lambda_e}{\lambda_p}=\sqrt{\dfrac{m_p}{m_e}}$ [1]
$=\sqrt{1836}\approx\boxed{42.8}$ (the electron's wavelength is larger) [1]

stem: State three features of the photoelectric effect that cannot be explained by the wave theory of light, and explain each using the photon picture.
model_answer:
Maximum kinetic energy depends on frequency, not intensity (wave: should grow with intensity). Photon: each electron gets one photon's energy $h u$, so $K_ ext{max}=h u-\phi_0$. [1]
There is a threshold frequency (wave: any frequency should work given enough intensity). Photon: if $h u<\phi_0$, no single photon can free an electron. [1]
Emission is instantaneous (wave: energy must accumulate over time). Photon: one photon is absorbed by one electron at once. [1]
